alt=\"Website\" data-canonical-src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/website-pgjev.com-0a56cf.svg\" style=\"max-width: 100%;\"\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWrite the condition the way you would say it. Postgres does the rest.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev\u003c/code\u003e lets you filter, rank and classify rows with plain-language conditions. Every row is judged by\n\u003ca href=\"https://docs.typesafe.ai\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eTypeSafe's Jev\u003c/a\u003e, a System One model that returns calibrated probabilities\ninstead of generated text. No index, no embeddings, no vector column.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWebsite: \u003ca href=\"https://pgjev.com\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003epgjev.com\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-sql notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"CREATE EXTENSION jev CASCADE;\n\nSELECT * FROM people WHERE jev(people, 'the name is European');\n\nSELECT subject, jev_prob(tickets, 'the customer is angry') AS p\nFROM tickets ORDER BY p DESC LIMIT 20;\n\nSELECT jev_choice(tickets, 'which team should handle this?',\n                  ARRAY['billing', 'technical', 'security', 'sales']) AS team, count(*)\nFROM tickets GROUP BY 1;\n\nSELECT name, jev_score(products, 'how luxurious is this product?',\n                       ARRAY['budget', 'mid-range', 'premium', 'luxury']) AS luxury\nFROM products ORDER BY luxury DESC;\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003eCREATE EXTENSION jev CASCADE;\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eSELECT\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e*\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eFROM\u003c/span\u003e people \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eWHERE\u003c/span\u003e jev(people, \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003ethe name is European\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e);\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eSELECT\u003c/span\u003e subject, jev_prob(tickets, \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003ethe customer is angry\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e) \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eAS\u003c/span\u003e p\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eFROM\u003c/span\u003e tickets \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eORDER BY\u003c/span\u003e p \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eDESC\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eLIMIT\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003e20\u003c/span\u003e;\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eSELECT\u003c/span\u003e jev_choice(tickets, \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003ewhich team should handle this?\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e,\n                  ARRAY[\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003ebilling\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e, \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003etechnical\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e, \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003esecurity\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e, \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003esales\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e]) \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eAS\u003c/span\u003e team, \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003ecount\u003c/span\u003e(\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e*\u003c/span\u003e)\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eFROM\u003c/span\u003e tickets \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eGROUP BY\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003e1\u003c/span\u003e;\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eSELECT\u003c/span\u003e name, jev_score(products, \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003ehow luxurious is this product?\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e,\n                       ARRAY[\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003ebudget\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e, \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003emid-range\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e, \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003epremium\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e, \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003eluxury\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e]) \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eAS\u003c/span\u003e luxury\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eFROM\u003c/span\u003e products \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eORDER BY\u003c/span\u003e luxury \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eDESC\u003c/span\u003e;\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev()\u003c/code\u003e is an ordinary boolean function, so it composes with everything else in SQL: \u003ccode\u003eAND age \u0026gt; 40\u003c/code\u003e,\njoins, \u003ccode\u003eGROUP BY\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eLIMIT\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eORDER BY jev_prob(...)\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eHow it works\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-how-it-works\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: How it works\" href=\"#how-it-works\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev(table, 'condition')\u003c/code\u003e receives the row as a composite value. The first call for a table + condition starts a\nread-ahead that streams the table in physical order (TID range scans; \u003ccode\u003eOFFSET\u003c/code\u003e pages for views), so memory stays\nconstant whatever the table size.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eRows are packed \u003ccode\u003ejev.batch_size\u003c/code\u003e (20) per request into one shared \u003cem\u003estate\u003c/em\u003e\n(\u003ccode\u003e{\"condition\": ..., \"rows\": [...]}\u003c/code\u003e) with one yes/no \u003ca href=\"https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eNoul\u003c/a\u003e\nquestion per row. Jev evaluates all questions over one state in parallel, which amortises the ~270-token\nrequest overhead (about 435 tokens for one row alone vs 175 per row in batches of 20).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eUp to 2 × \u003ccode\u003ejev.concurrency\u003c/code\u003e requests are in flight over persistent HTTPS connections, and every row is answered\nas soon as its batch returns, so a \u003ccode\u003eLIMIT\u003c/code\u003e stops the read-ahead after the in-flight window, and rows that cheaper\npredicates filter out before \u003ccode\u003ejev()\u003c/code\u003e runs (\u003ccode\u003eWHERE age \u0026gt; 60 AND jev(...)\u003c/code\u003e) are skipped rather than judged.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAnswers are cached per row content for the session, so re-running, changing the threshold or sorting by\nprobability is free. Rows from a subquery or CTE (anonymous \u003ccode\u003erecord\u003c/code\u003e type) can't be read ahead and are judged\none request at a time; put \u003ccode\u003ejev()\u003c/code\u003e on base tables or views when you can.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMeasured on a 2,000-row table from Europe (~190 ms to the API): first run ≈ 3.5 s in 100 requests, ≈ 296k input\ntokens, ≈ $0.012; second run ≈ 50 ms; \u003ccode\u003eLIMIT 3\u003c/code\u003e on a new condition ≈ 0.6 s. A new condition in a session that\nstill holds its pooled connections (idle for less than \u003ccode\u003ejev.keepalive\u003c/code\u003e) takes ≈ 2.3 s: the first request on each\nfresh connection is the slow one. Version 0.1.0 needed 8.5 s (and 338k tokens) for the full query and 8.4 s for\nthe \u003ccode\u003eLIMIT\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhy 20 rows per request\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-why-20-rows-per-request\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Why 20 rows per request\" href=\"#why-20-rows-per-request\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eJev has to find \u003ccode\u003erows[i]\u003c/code\u003e by position in the array, and that gets unreliable in long arrays. Against ground truth\nfrom structured columns (job title, EU membership, a phrase in a free-text field; 400 rows each), batches of 1–20\nrows were 100 % correct, batches of 40 were 92–98 % and batches of 80 were 77–94 %. Wider rows (1,000 characters)\nmade no difference at 20. Naming rows instead of indexing them did not help. Batches of 20 cost 4 % more tokens than\nbatches of 40 and are just as fast, because a request's latency barely depends on its size.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eInstall\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-install\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Install\" href=\"#install\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eRequirements: PostgreSQL 14–17 with \u003ccode\u003eplpython3u\u003c/code\u003e (package \u003ccode\u003epostgresql-plpython3-NN\u003c/code\u003e on Debian/Ubuntu,\nincluded in the EDB and Postgres.app builds), a superuser, and a TypeSafe API key from \u003ca href=\"https://console.typesafe.ai\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003ehttps://console.typesafe.ai\u003c/a\u003e.\nManaged hosts that withhold superuser or \u003ccode\u003eplpython3u\u003c/code\u003e (Supabase, Neon, RDS, …) cannot run it; see\n\u003ca href=\"https://pgjev.com/docs/getting-started/where-it-runs\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eWhere it runs\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWith an AI agent (easiest)\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-with-an-ai-agent-easiest\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: With an AI agent (easiest)\" href=\"#with-an-ai-agent-easiest\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe repo ships an \u003ca href=\"/realZachi/pg-jev/blob/master/.agents/skills/pgjev/SKILL.md\"\u003eagent skill\u003c/a\u003e on \u003ca href=\"https://skills.sh\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eskills.sh\u003c/a\u003e. Install it into\nyour project and tell Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any other skill-aware agent to finish the job:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"npx skills add realZachi/pg-jev\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003enpx skills add realZachi/pg-jev\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eInstall pgjev on this server and set it up.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe agent runs a preflight (PostgreSQL version, \u003ccode\u003eplpython3u\u003c/code\u003e, superuser), \u003ccode\u003epgxn install jev\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003emake install\u003c/code\u003e against the right\n\u003ccode\u003epg_config\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eCREATE EXTENSION jev CASCADE\u003c/code\u003e, places the API key and runs a smoke test. Afterwards it also knows how\nto write cost-conscious \u003ccode\u003ejev()\u003c/code\u003e queries (\"find the tickets where the customer threatens to cancel\") and to explain\nwhat pgjev can do. The docs are readable as Markdown for agents too: append \u003ccode\u003e.md\u003c/code\u003e to any page under\n\u003ca href=\"https://pgjev.com/docs\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003ehttps://pgjev.com/docs\u003c/a\u003e (see \u003ca href=\"https://pgjev.com/docs/for-agents\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eFor agents\u003c/a\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv are plain GUCs: \u003ccode\u003eSET jev.\u0026lt;name\u0026gt; = ...\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eALTER ROLE ... SET\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eALTER DATABASE ... SET\u003c/code\u003e, or \u003ccode\u003epostgresql.conf\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eSetting\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eDefault\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eMeaning\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev.api_key\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eenv \u003ccode\u003eTYPESAFE_API_KEY\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eTypeSafe API key\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev.model\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev-latest\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eModel name or pinned version such as \u003ccode\u003ejev-1.13.0\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev.threshold\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e0.5\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eProbability at which \u003ccode\u003ejev()\u003c/code\u003e returns true\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev.batch_size\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e20\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eRows per API request. Accuracy drops measurably above ~20–25 (see above)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev.concurrency\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e16\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eParallel API requests; up to twice that many are queued ahead of the executor\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev.max_prefetch_rows\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e5000\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eHow far past a cache miss the read-ahead scans to find the requested row, and how many skipped rows it keeps for later requests (memory bound)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev.notices\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eon\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eEmit a progress \u003ccode\u003eNOTICE\u003c/code\u003e per finished request and a summary per table with request count, tokens, estimated cost and time\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev.api_url\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ehttps://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eEndpoint (proxies, mocks)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev.timeout\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e30\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eSeconds per API request. Waits are interruptible: \u003ccode\u003estatement_timeout\u003c/code\u003e and cancel requests apply within 250 ms\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev.keepalive\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e600\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eSeconds a pooled API connection may sit idle before it is reconnected. The first request on a fresh connection costs a TLS handshake plus, measured, up to 1.5 s of server-side setup, so keep connections alive across queries; TCP keepalive probes catch silently dropped ones\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev.max_rows_per_statement\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e0\u003c/code\u003e (off)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAbort a statement that would send more rows than this to the API. Spend guard for shared deployments\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev.max_chars_per_statement\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e0\u003c/code\u003e (off)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eSame, for characters of row data\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWriting good conditions\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-writing-good-conditions\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Writing good conditions\" href=\"#writing-good-conditions\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eJev answers the question you wrote, literally. A few things that help (more in the\n\u003ca href=\"https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eTypeSafe docs\u003c/a\u003e):\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eState the exact condition: \u003ccode\u003e'the customer threatens to leave, dispute a charge, or take legal action'\u003c/code\u003e\nbeats \u003ccode\u003e'churn risk'\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eKeep arithmetic, dates and exact matches in SQL; let the model judge meaning.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eLook at the distribution with \u003ccode\u003ejev_prob()\u003c/code\u003e before picking a threshold. Ambiguous cases really do land\nnear 0.5.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSend only the columns the judgment needs: create a view with the relevant columns (and any pre-filter) and call\n\u003ccode\u003ejev(view_alias, ...)\u003c/code\u003e on the view. Views are read ahead and batched like tables.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eCaveats\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-caveats\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Caveats\" href=\"#caveats\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThis is a full scan by design: every row the executor asks about goes to the API. Cheaper predicates in the same\n\u003ccode\u003eWHERE\u003c/code\u003e run first and their rejects are skipped; a \u003ccode\u003eLIMIT\u003c/code\u003e stops early; \u003ccode\u003ejev.max_rows_per_statement\u003c/code\u003e caps spend.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eRow contents are sent to a third-party API. Do not use it on data you may not share.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThe cache lives in the backend session (PL/Python \u003ccode\u003eGD\u003c/code\u003e). Connection pools with many sessions each warm their\nown cache.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eplpython3u\u003c/code\u003e is an untrusted language: only superusers can create the extension, and functions run with the\nserver's OS privileges.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eDevelopment\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-development\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Development\" href=\"#development\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"make docker-test                 # builds test/Dockerfile and runs the regression suite (PG_MAJOR=16 by default)\nmake docker-test PG_MAJOR=17\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003emake docker-test                 \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e builds test/Dockerfile and runs the regression suite (PG_MAJOR=16 by default)\u003c/span\u003e\nmake docker-test PG_MAJOR=17\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eLocally with a running server and \u003ccode\u003epg_config\u003c/code\u003e on \u003ccode\u003ePATH\u003c/code\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"make install\npython3 test/mock_api.py \u0026amp;       # deterministic stand-in for the TypeSafe API\nmake installcheck                # pg_regress, tests in test/sql, expected output in test/expected\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003emake install\npython3 test/mock_api.py \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026amp;\u003c/span\u003e       \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e deterministic stand-in for the TypeSafe API\u003c/span\u003e\nmake installcheck                \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e pg_regress, tests in test/sql, expected output in test/expected\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe regression tests never call the live API. To try the real thing, \u003ccode\u003eSET jev.api_key\u003c/code\u003e and run any query.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSee \u003ca href=\"/realZachi/pg-jev/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md\"\u003eCONTRIBUTING.md\u003c/a\u003e and \u003ca href=\"/realZachi/pg-jev/blob/master/docs/PUBLISHING.md\"\u003edocs/PUBLISHING.md\u003c/a\u003e for release steps.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eLicense\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-license\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: License\" href=\"#license\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"/realZachi/pg-jev/blob/master/LICENSE\"\u003ePostgreSQL License\u003c/a\u003e. class="markdown-body entry-content container-lg" itemprop="text"><p align="center" dir="auto">
  <a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/realZachi/pg-jev/blob/master/docs/assets/header.svg"><img src="/realZachi/pg-jev/raw/master/docs/assets/header.svg" alt="pg-jev — ask your Postgres tables questions in plain language" width="100%" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h1 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">jev — ask your Postgres tables questions in plain language</h1><a id="user-content-jev--ask-your-postgres-tables-questions-in-plain-language" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: jev — ask your Postgres tables questions in plain language" href="#jev--ask-your-postgres-tables-questions-in-plain-language"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://github.com/realZachi/pg-jev/actions/workflows/ci.yml"><img src="https://github.com/realZachi/pg-jev/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg" alt="CI" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
<a href="https://pgxn.org/dist/jev/" rel="nofollow"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/815f0dbea840e2ac92aed4f1333110ef98ba5542af98fe864f19ca21eb98334f/68747470733a2f2f62616467652e667572792e696f2f70672f6a65762e737667" alt="PGXN" data-canonical-src="https://badge.fury.io/pg/jev.svg" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
<a href="/realZachi/pg-jev/blob/master/LICENSE"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/195f9bd195fbd9bab7df6a247d175ac8b60ddec0770c73a611554d0f8df09edd/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f6c6963656e73652d506f737467726553514c2d626c75652e737667" alt="License" data-canonical-src="https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PostgreSQL-blue.svg" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
<a href="https://pgjev.com" rel="nofollow"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/ea4dc3ebce7141940d1a1e7dc6a5691ddf34f422fe6d378b34357167440670ed/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f776562736974652d70676a65762e636f6d2d3061353663662e737667" alt="Website" data-canonical-src="https://img.shields.io/badge/website-pgjev.com-0a56cf.svg" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto">Write the condition the way you would say it. Postgres does the rest.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>jev</code> lets you filter, rank and classify rows with plain-language conditions. Every row is judged by
<a href="https://docs.typesafe.ai" rel="nofollow">TypeSafe's Jev</a>, a System One model that returns calibrated probabilities
instead of generated text. No index, no embeddings, no vector column.</p>
<p dir="auto">Website: <a href="https://pgjev.com" rel="nofollow">pgjev.com</a></p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-sql notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="CREATE EXTENSION jev CASCADE;

SELECT * FROM people WHERE jev(people, 'the name is European');

SELECT subject, jev_prob(tickets, 'the customer is angry') AS p
FROM tickets ORDER BY p DESC LIMIT 20;

SELECT jev_choice(tickets, 'which team should handle this?',
                  ARRAY['billing', 'technical', 'security', 'sales']) AS team, count(*)
FROM tickets GROUP BY 1;

SELECT name, jev_score(products, 'how luxurious is this product?',
                       ARRAY['budget', 'mid-range', 'premium', 'luxury']) AS luxury
FROM products ORDER BY luxury DESC;"><pre>CREATE EXTENSION jev CASCADE;

<span class="pl-k">SELECT</span> <span class="pl-k">*</span> <span class="pl-k">FROM</span> people <span class="pl-k">WHERE</span> jev(people, <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>the name is European<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>);

<span class="pl-k">SELECT</span> subject, jev_prob(tickets, <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>the customer is angry<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>) <span class="pl-k">AS</span> p
<span class="pl-k">FROM</span> tickets <span class="pl-k">ORDER BY</span> p <span class="pl-k">DESC</span> <span class="pl-k">LIMIT</span> <span class="pl-c1">20</span>;

<span class="pl-k">SELECT</span> jev_choice(tickets, <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>which team should handle this?<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>,
                  ARRAY[<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>billing<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>, <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>technical<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>, <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>security<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>, <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>sales<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>]) <span class="pl-k">AS</span> team, <span class="pl-c1">count</span>(<span class="pl-k">*</span>)
<span class="pl-k">FROM</span> tickets <span class="pl-k">GROUP BY</span> <span class="pl-c1">1</span>;

<span class="pl-k">SELECT</span> name, jev_score(products, <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>how luxurious is this product?<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>,
                       ARRAY[<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>budget<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>, <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>mid-range<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>, <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>premium<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>, <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>luxury<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>]) <span class="pl-k">AS</span> luxury
<span class="pl-k">FROM</span> products <span class="pl-k">ORDER BY</span> luxury <span class="pl-k">DESC</span>;</pre></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>jev()</code> is an ordinary boolean function, so it composes with everything else in SQL: <code>AND age &gt; 40</code>,
joins, <code>GROUP BY</code>, <code>LIMIT</code>, <code>ORDER BY jev_prob(...)</code>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">How it works</h2><a id="user-content-how-it-works" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: How it works" href="#how-it-works"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><code>jev(table, 'condition')</code> receives the row as a composite value. The first call for a table + condition starts a
read-ahead that streams the table in physical order (TID range scans; <code>OFFSET</code> pages for views), so memory stays
constant whatever the table size.</li>
<li>Rows are packed <code>jev.batch_size</code> (20) per request into one shared <em>state</em>
(<code>{"condition": ..., "rows": [...]}</code>) with one yes/no <a href="https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul" rel="nofollow">Noul</a>
question per row. Jev evaluates all questions over one state in parallel, which amortises the ~270-token
request overhead (about 435 tokens for one row alone vs 175 per row in batches of 20).</li>
<li>Up to 2 × <code>jev.concurrency</code> requests are in flight over persistent HTTPS connections, and every row is answered
as soon as its batch returns, so a <code>LIMIT</code> stops the read-ahead after the in-flight window, and rows that cheaper
predicates filter out before <code>jev()</code> runs (<code>WHERE age &gt; 60 AND jev(...)</code>) are skipped rather than judged.</li>
<li>Answers are cached per row content for the session, so re-running, changing the threshold or sorting by
probability is free. Rows from a subquery or CTE (anonymous <code>record</code> type) can't be read ahead and are judged
one request at a time; put <code>jev()</code> on base tables or views when you can.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Measured on a 2,000-row table from Europe (~190 ms to the API): first run ≈ 3.5 s in 100 requests, ≈ 296k input
tokens, ≈ $0.012; second run ≈ 50 ms; <code>LIMIT 3</code> on a new condition ≈ 0.6 s. A new condition in a session that
still holds its pooled connections (idle for less than <code>jev.keepalive</code>) takes ≈ 2.3 s: the first request on each
fresh connection is the slow one. Version 0.1.0 needed 8.5 s (and 338k tokens) for the full query and 8.4 s for
the <code>LIMIT</code>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why 20 rows per request</h3><a id="user-content-why-20-rows-per-request" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why 20 rows per request" href="#why-20-rows-per-request"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Jev has to find <code>rows[i]</code> by position in the array, and that gets unreliable in long arrays. Against ground truth
from structured columns (job title, EU membership, a phrase in a free-text field; 400 rows each), batches of 1–20
rows were 100 % correct, batches of 40 were 92–98 % and batches of 80 were 77–94 %. Wider rows (1,000 characters)
made no difference at 20. Naming rows instead of indexing them did not help. Batches of 20 cost 4 % more tokens than
batches of 40 and are just as fast, because a request's latency barely depends on its size.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Install</h2><a id="user-content-install" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Install" href="#install"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Requirements: PostgreSQL 14–17 with <code>plpython3u</code> (package <code>postgresql-plpython3-NN</code> on Debian/Ubuntu,
included in the EDB and Postgres.app builds), a superuser, and a TypeSafe API key from <a href="https://console.typesafe.ai" rel="nofollow">https://console.typesafe.ai</a>.
Managed hosts that withhold superuser or <code>plpython3u</code> (Supabase, Neon, RDS, …) cannot run it; see
<a href="https://pgjev.com/docs/getting-started/where-it-runs" rel="nofollow">Where it runs</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">With an AI agent (easiest)</h3><a id="user-content-with-an-ai-agent-easiest" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: With an AI agent (easiest)" href="#with-an-ai-agent-easiest"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The repo ships an <a href="/realZachi/pg-jev/blob/master/.agents/skills/pgjev/SKILL.md">agent skill</a> on <a href="https://skills.sh" rel="nofollow">skills.sh</a>. Install it into
your project and tell Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any other skill-aware agent to finish the job:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="npx skills add realZachi/pg-jev"><pre>npx skills add realZachi/pg-jev</pre></div>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Install pgjev on this server and set it up.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">The agent runs a preflight (PostgreSQL version, <code>plpython3u</code>, superuser), <code>pgxn install jev</code> or <code>make install</code> against the right
<code>pg_config</code>, <code>CREATE EXTENSION jev CASCADE</code>, places the API key and runs a smoke test. Afterwards it also knows how
to write cost-conscious <code>jev()</code> queries ("find the tickets where the customer threatens to cancel") and to explain
what pgjev can do. The docs are readable as Markdown for agents too: append <code>.md</code> to any page under
<a href="https://pgjev.com/docs" rel="nofollow">https://pgjev.com/docs</a> (see <a href="https://pgjev.com/docs/for-agents" rel="nofollow">For agents</a>).</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">From PGXN</h3><a id="user-content-from-pgxn" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: From PGXN" href="#from-pgxn"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="pip install pgxnclient       # once; also available as `pgxn-client` in Debian/Ubuntu and Homebrew
pgxn install jev             # downloads the release from pgxn.org and runs `make install` against pg_config on PATH
psql -c &quot;CREATE EXTENSION jev CASCADE&quot;"><pre>pip install pgxnclient       <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> once; also available as `pgxn-client` in Debian/Ubuntu and Homebrew</span>
pgxn install jev             <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> downloads the release from pgxn.org and runs `make install` against pg_config on PATH</span>
psql -c <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>CREATE EXTENSION jev CASCADE<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Use <code>pgxn install jev --pg_config=/path/to/pg_config</code> (or <code>sudo pgxn install jev</code>) when the server's <code>pg_config</code>
is not on PATH or the extension directory is not writable.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">From source (PGXS)</h3><a id="user-content-from-source-pgxs" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: From source (PGXS)" href="#from-source-pgxs"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="git clone https://github.com/realZachi/pg-jev.git &amp;&amp; cd pg-jev
make install            # uses pg_config on PATH; or: make install PG_CONFIG=/path/to/pg_config
psql -c &quot;CREATE EXTENSION jev CASCADE&quot;   # superuser required (plpython3u is untrusted); CASCADE creates plpython3u"><pre>git clone https://github.com/realZachi/pg-jev.git <span class="pl-k">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="pl-c1">cd</span> pg-jev
make install            <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> uses pg_config on PATH; or: make install PG_CONFIG=/path/to/pg_config</span>
psql -c <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>CREATE EXTENSION jev CASCADE<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>   <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> superuser required (plpython3u is untrusted); CASCADE creates plpython3u</span></pre></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Docker</h3><a id="user-content-docker" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Docker" href="#docker"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="docker build -t pg-jev .                       # add --build-arg PG_MAJOR=17 for another major

psql postgres://postgres:pw@localhost/postgres -c &quot;CREATE EXTENSION jev CASCADE&quot;"><pre>docker build -t pg-jev <span class="pl-c1">.</span>                       <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> add --build-arg PG_MAJOR=17 for another major</span>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">API key</h3><a id="user-content-api-key" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: API key" href="#api-key"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Either export <code>TYPESAFE_API_KEY</code> in the environment of the PostgreSQL server process, or set it per session
or per role:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-sql notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="SET jev.api_key = 'your-key';
ALTER ROLE analyst SET jev.api_key = 'your-key';   -- persistent, per role"><pre><span class="pl-k">SET</span> <span class="pl-c1">jev</span>.<span class="pl-c1">api_key</span> <span class="pl-k">=</span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>your-key<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>;
ALTER ROLE analyst <span class="pl-k">SET</span> <span class="pl-c1">jev</span>.<span class="pl-c1">api_key</span> <span class="pl-k">=</span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>your-key<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>;   <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">--</span> persistent, per role</span></pre></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Functions</h2><a id="user-content-functions" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Functions" href="#functions"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Function</th>
<th>Returns</th>
<th>Purpose</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>jev(row, condition [, threshold])</code></td>
<td>boolean</td>
<td><code>WHERE</code> predicate. Threshold: argument → <code>jev.threshold</code> → 0.5</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev_prob(row, condition)</code></td>
<td>float8</td>
<td>Probability 0..1 that the row satisfies the condition</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev_score(row, question, levels text[])</code></td>
<td>float8</td>
<td>Probability-weighted position on ordered levels (0 .. n-1)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev_score_norm(row, question, levels)</code></td>
<td>float8</td>
<td>Same, normalised to 0..1</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev_choice(row, question, options text[])</code></td>
<td>text</td>
<td>The most likely option for the row</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev_confidence(row, question, kind, options)</code></td>
<td>float8</td>
<td>Confidence of a <code>score</code>/<code>choice</code> answer</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev_eval(row, question, kind, options)</code></td>
<td>jsonb</td>
<td>Full raw answer (probabilities, legend, confidence)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev_stats()</code></td>
<td>jsonb</td>
<td>Requests, tokens, estimated cost, cache hits, in-flight requests and pooled connections for this session</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev_cache_clear()</code></td>
<td>void</td>
<td>Forget cached judgments</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev_version()</code></td>
<td>text</td>
<td>Extension version</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto"><code>row</code> is the table alias itself (<code>jev(people, ...)</code>) or a subquery alias.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Settings</h2><a id="user-content-settings" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Settings" href="#settings"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">All settings are plain GUCs: <code>SET jev.&lt;name&gt; = ...</code>, <code>ALTER ROLE ... SET</code>, <code>ALTER DATABASE ... SET</code>, or <code>postgresql.conf</code>.</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Setting</th>
<th>Default</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>jev.api_key</code></td>
<td>env <code>TYPESAFE_API_KEY</code></td>
<td>TypeSafe API key</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev.model</code></td>
<td><code>jev-latest</code></td>
<td>Model name or pinned version such as <code>jev-1.13.0</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev.threshold</code></td>
<td><code>0.5</code></td>
<td>Probability at which <code>jev()</code> returns true</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev.batch_size</code></td>
<td><code>20</code></td>
<td>Rows per API request. Accuracy drops measurably above ~20–25 (see above)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev.concurrency</code></td>
<td><code>16</code></td>
<td>Parallel API requests; up to twice that many are queued ahead of the executor</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev.max_prefetch_rows</code></td>
<td><code>5000</code></td>
<td>How far past a cache miss the read-ahead scans to find the requested row, and how many skipped rows it keeps for later requests (memory bound)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev.notices</code></td>
<td><code>on</code></td>
<td>Emit a progress <code>NOTICE</code> per finished request and a summary per table with request count, tokens, estimated cost and time</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev.api_url</code></td>
<td><code>https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone</code></td>
<td>Endpoint (proxies, mocks)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev.timeout</code></td>
<td><code>30</code></td>
<td>Seconds per API request. Waits are interruptible: <code>statement_timeout</code> and cancel requests apply within 250 ms</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev.keepalive</code></td>
<td><code>600</code></td>
<td>Seconds a pooled API connection may sit idle before it is reconnected. The first request on a fresh connection costs a TLS handshake plus, measured, up to 1.5 s of server-side setup, so keep connections alive across queries; TCP keepalive probes catch silently dropped ones</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev.max_rows_per_statement</code></td>
<td><code>0</code> (off)</td>
<td>Abort a statement that would send more rows than this to the API. Spend guard for shared deployments</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev.max_chars_per_statement</code></td>
<td><code>0</code> (off)</td>
<td>Same, for characters of row data</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Writing good conditions</h2><a id="user-content-writing-good-conditions" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Writing good conditions" href="#writing-good-conditions"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Jev answers the question you wrote, literally. A few things that help (more in the
<a href="https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13" rel="nofollow">TypeSafe docs</a>):</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>State the exact condition: <code>'the customer threatens to leave, dispute a charge, or take legal action'</code>
beats <code>'churn risk'</code>.</li>
<li>Keep arithmetic, dates and exact matches in SQL; let the model judge meaning.</li>
<li>Look at the distribution with <code>jev_prob()</code> before picking a threshold. Ambiguous cases really do land
near 0.5.</li>
<li>Send only the columns the judgment needs: create a view with the relevant columns (and any pre-filter) and call
<code>jev(view_alias, ...)</code> on the view. Views are read ahead and batched like tables.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Caveats</h2><a id="user-content-caveats" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Caveats" href="#caveats"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>This is a full scan by design: every row the executor asks about goes to the API. Cheaper predicates in the same
<code>WHERE</code> run first and their rejects are skipped; a <code>LIMIT</code> stops early; <code>jev.max_rows_per_statement</code> caps spend.</li>
<li>Row contents are sent to a third-party API. Do not use it on data you may not share.</li>
<li>The cache lives in the backend session (PL/Python <code>GD</code>). Connection pools with many sessions each warm their
own cache.</li>
<li><code>plpython3u</code> is an untrusted language: only superusers can create the extension, and functions run with the
server's OS privileges.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Development</h2><a id="user-content-development" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Development" href="#development"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="make docker-test                 # builds test/Dockerfile and runs the regression suite (PG_MAJOR=16 by default)
make docker-test PG_MAJOR=17"><pre>make docker-test                 <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> builds test/Dockerfile and runs the regression suite (PG_MAJOR=16 by default)</span>
make docker-test PG_MAJOR=17</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Locally with a running server and <code>pg_config</code> on <code>PATH</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="make install
python3 test/mock_api.py &amp;       # deterministic stand-in for the TypeSafe API
make installcheck                # pg_regress, tests in test/sql, expected output in test/expected"><pre>make install
python3 test/mock_api.py <span class="pl-k">&amp;</span>       <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> deterministic stand-in for the TypeSafe API</span>
make installcheck                <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> pg_regress, tests in test/sql, expected output in test/expected</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The regression tests never call the live API. To try the real thing, <code>SET jev.api_key</code> and run any query.</p>
<p dir="auto">See <a href="/realZachi/pg-jev/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md">CONTRIBUTING.md</a> and <a href="/realZachi/pg-jev/blob/master/docs/PUBLISHING.md">docs/PUBLISHING.md</a> for release steps.</p>
